name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.finiteDimensional_space_of_singleton_amongNonUnital
title: Finite-dimensional representation space in the unital singleton case

content.display_title: Finite-dimensional representation space in the unital singleton case
content.one_sentence_role: Applies the unital finite-dimensional-space theorem after checking the representation-interface conversion.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ satisfy the singleton condition of R11. Then $H$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb C$.
content.assumptions: The universal condition quantifies over every nonzero irreducible $*$-representation of $A$; representations presented without a unit equation are unital by irreducibility, as explained in R11.
content.conclusion: The same representation space $H$ has a finite complex basis.
content.proof_summary: Convert the comparison condition for the same representation and apply the finite-dimensional-space theorem.
proof_steps: Apply [The all-representations singleton condition implies the unital singleton condition](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/OrdinarySingleton.lean#L48-L63) to $\pi$. For a unital nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho$, write $\rho_0(a)=\rho(a)$ for the same operator map viewed through the interface that does not require a unit equation. The assumed condition then supplies a unitary $U$ with $U\pi(a)=\rho(a)U$ for every $a\in A$. Hence $\pi$ satisfies the unital singleton condition.

Apply [Finite dimension of the unital singleton representation space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/FiniteDimension.lean#L24-L66) to the same nonzero ordered unital $A$, same separable $H$, and same $\pi$ with that converted condition. Its conclusion is $\dim_{\mathbb C}H<\infty$. In that theorem the closed compact-preimage ideal becomes all of $A$, so $\pi(1)=I_H$ is compact and the compact-identity criterion supplies the finite dimension.
